drivers.title: Atlas consumption expansion
drivers.thesis: Atlas revenue is recognized on measured consumption; continued workload migration and new application demand raise consumed workload, while disclosed macro pressure slows the growth of existing applications.
causal_chain: Existing and new applications consume more database workload
Consumed usage is billed monthly in arrears
Usage-based revenue is recognized as the service is delivered
Atlas-related revenue grows at the modelled rate
drivers.persistence_rationale: Consumption growth has persisted for three audited years but the issuer discloses macro-driven slowing of existing applications, so persistence is not assumed structural.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: Atlas revenue is usage-based and billed in arrears, so consumption is the recognized-revenue driver.
Atlas rose to 70% of total revenue from 63% two years earlier, evidencing sustained consumption growth.
The issuer reports slower-than-historical growth of existing Atlas applications.

leading_indicators: Quarterly Atlas consumption growth disclosed in later filings
Remaining performance obligations recognised within twelve months
falsifiers: Atlas revenue growth below 7% in any forecast year
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: The filing itself discloses macro-driven slowing of existing Atlas applications; the low case is built around that headwind rather than dismissed.

drivers.title: Enterprise estate and large-cohort expansion
drivers.thesis: Growth in Direct Sales Customers and in the at-least-$100,000 ARR cohort supports term-license and support revenue, whose growth is far slower than Atlas.
causal_chain: Direct sales expands the enterprise customer count
Large customers standardize additional workloads
Term licences and support renew and expand
Other subscription revenue grows modestly
drivers.persistence_rationale: Customer counts grew each year, but the disclosed category grew only 3.2% in FY2025 as customers migrated workloads to Atlas, so expansion is modelled as low growth.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: Direct Sales Customers grew from over 6,400 to over 7,500 in two years.
Customers with at least $100,000 of ARR or annualized MRR rose to 2,396.

falsifiers: Other subscription revenue declining in the base case
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: The filing discloses customer-count expansion and single-digit category growth; no contrary evidence on the enterprise base was found within the opened filing.

drivers.title: Contracted backlog and deferred-revenue conversion
drivers.thesis: Remaining performance obligations and deferred revenue give bounded visibility into near-term recognized revenue, including services delivered alongside deployments.
causal_chain: Contracted backlog and deferred revenue are carried into the period
Obligations are satisfied as services are delivered
Previously deferred amounts are recognized as revenue
Services and support revenue is partly supported by that stock
drivers.persistence_rationale: Backlog is a bounded stock that converts within roughly three years; it supports the near-term path but is not a multi-year growth mechanism.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: 748.0 USD million of remaining performance obligations existed at FY2025 year end, 59% due within twelve months.
18% of FY2025 revenue came from deferred revenue outstanding at the start of the period.

leading_indicators: Remaining performance obligations at each period end
falsifiers: Services revenue contracting while backlog grows
Backlog conversion slower than the disclosed twelve-month share
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: No independent evidence on services attach or backlog cancellation was read; the high case could therefore be exceeded or missed without a checked signal.

drivers.title: Atlas consumption expansion
drivers.thesis: Atlas revenue is recognized on measured consumption; continued workload migration and new application demand raise consumed workload, while disclosed macro pressure slows the growth of existing applications.
causal_chain: Existing and new applications consume more database workload
Consumed usage is billed monthly in arrears
Usage-based revenue is recognized as the service is delivered
Atlas-related revenue grows at the modelled rate
drivers.persistence_rationale: Consumption growth has persisted for three audited years but the issuer discloses macro-driven slowing of existing applications, so persistence is not assumed structural.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: Atlas revenue is usage-based and billed in arrears, so consumption is the recognized-revenue driver.
Atlas rose to 70% of total revenue from 63% two years earlier, evidencing sustained consumption growth.
The issuer reports slower-than-historical growth of existing Atlas applications.

leading_indicators: Quarterly Atlas consumption growth disclosed in later filings
Remaining performance obligations recognised within twelve months
falsifiers: Atlas revenue growth below 7% in any forecast year
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: The filing itself discloses macro-driven slowing of existing Atlas applications; the low case is built around that headwind rather than dismissed.

drivers.title: Enterprise estate and large-cohort expansion
drivers.thesis: Growth in Direct Sales Customers and in the at-least-$100,000 ARR cohort supports term-license and support revenue, whose growth is far slower than Atlas.
causal_chain: Direct sales expands the enterprise customer count
Large customers standardize additional workloads
Term licences and support renew and expand
Other subscription revenue grows modestly
drivers.persistence_rationale: Customer counts grew each year, but the disclosed category grew only 3.2% in FY2025 as customers migrated workloads to Atlas, so expansion is modelled as low growth.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: Direct Sales Customers grew from over 6,400 to over 7,500 in two years.
Customers with at least $100,000 of ARR or annualized MRR rose to 2,396.

falsifiers: Other subscription revenue declining in the base case
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: The filing discloses customer-count expansion and single-digit category growth; no contrary evidence on the enterprise base was found within the opened filing.

drivers.title: Contracted backlog and deferred-revenue conversion
drivers.thesis: Remaining performance obligations and deferred revenue give bounded visibility into near-term recognized revenue, including services delivered alongside deployments.
causal_chain: Contracted backlog and deferred revenue are carried into the period
Obligations are satisfied as services are delivered
Previously deferred amounts are recognized as revenue
Services and support revenue is partly supported by that stock
drivers.persistence_rationale: Backlog is a bounded stock that converts within roughly three years; it supports the near-term path but is not a multi-year growth mechanism.

evidence_nodes.conclusion: 748.0 USD million of remaining performance obligations existed at FY2025 year end, 59% due within twelve months.
18% of FY2025 revenue came from deferred revenue outstanding at the start of the period.

leading_indicators: Remaining performance obligations at each period end
falsifiers: Services revenue contracting while backlog grows
Backlog conversion slower than the disclosed twelve-month share
drivers.counterevidence_rationale: No independent evidence on services attach or backlog cancellation was read; the high case could therefore be exceeded or missed without a checked signal.

growth_driver_tree.rationale: One root per disclosed revenue category: each root maps only to that category's Base growth parameters, and the weights are analyst allocations rather than identified causal effects.
